project.projectDesc: Combines purchase, session, and user data to explore player-value prediction and behavioral segmentation.

caseStudy.summary: This academic game-analytics project combines purchase, session, and user records to study customer lifetime value and player segmentation. The notebook aggregates behavior by user and explores regression approaches for estimating value and supporting marketing analysis.
caseStudy.challenge: Game activity is recorded across purchase, session, and user tables, so useful analysis depends on joining events into consistent player-level features. The project explores how those features can support value estimation and behavioral segmentation.
caseStudy.architecture: The notebook aggregates purchase and session records by user identifier, joins them with user data, and applies regression approaches including linear regression and Lasso. The resulting features and estimates support player-value and segment analysis.
caseStudy.diagram:
flowchart LR
  Purchases[Purchase records] --> Aggregate[Aggregate by player]
  Sessions[Session records] --> Aggregate
  Users[User records] --> Join[Player feature table]
  Aggregate --> Join
  Join --> Models[Regression and Lasso]
  Models --> Segments[Value and behavior analysis]
contributions: Built notebook workflows to aggregate purchase, session, and user records by player.
Joined the resulting tables into analysis-ready player features.
Explored linear regression, Lasso, and Keras modeling approaches.
Connected value estimates and behavior patterns to player-segmentation questions.
tradeoffs: Player-level aggregation simplifies behavioral analysis but depends on careful feature definitions and time windows.
Linear and regularized models provide useful baselines, while more complex models require stronger validation and interpretability checks.
